sanskrit: tato mohaṃ samāpanne tanaye mama bhārata mumoca bāṇāṃs tvaritaḥ punar anyān durāsadān
english: Then, when stupor had overcome my son, O Bhārata, he swiftly released yet more arrows, difficult to withstand.

sanskrit: sa tair abhihato bāṇair bahubhis tena mohitaḥ niśceṣṭaḥ kauravaśreṣṭha pradyumno 'bhūd raṇājire
english: Struck by those many arrows and bewildered by him, Pradyumna lay motionless on the battlefield, O best of the Kauravas.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca śālvabāṇārdite tasmin pradyumne balināṃ vare vṛṣṇayo bhagnasaṃkalpā vivyathuḥ pṛtanāgatāḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: When that Pradyumna, best among the mighty, was tormented by Śālva's arrows, the Vṛṣṇis who had come to battle trembled, their resolve broken.

sanskrit: hāhākṛtam abhūt sārvaṃ vṛṣṇyandhakabalaṃ tadā pradyumne patite rājan pare ca muditābhavan
english: The entire army of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas raised cries of grief when Pradyumna fell, O king, while the enemies rejoiced.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā mohitaṃ dṛṣṭvā sārathir javanair hayaiḥ raṇād apāharat tūrṇaṃ śikṣito dārukis tataḥ
english: Seeing him thus bewildered, the trained charioteer Daruki swiftly carried him away from the battle with swift horses.

sanskrit: nātidūrāpayāte tu rathe rathavarapraṇut dhanur gṛhītvā yantāraṃ labdhasaṃjño 'bravīd idam
english: When the chariot had gone not too far, the driver of the best of chariots regained his senses, grasped his bow, and spoke these words to the charioteer.

sanskrit: saute kiṃ te vyavasitaṃ kasmād yāsi parāṅmukhaḥ naiṣa vṛṣṇipravīrāṇām āhave dharma ucyate
english: "O charioteer, what is your intention? Why do you go with your back to the enemy? This is not declared the duty of the Vṛṣṇi heroes in battle.

sanskrit: kaccit saute na te mohaḥ śālvaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahāhave viṣādo vā raṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā brūhi me tvaṃ yathātatham
english: "Is there no confusion in you, O charioteer, upon seeing Śālva in the great battle? Or depression upon seeing the combat? Tell me the truth.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca jānārdane na me moho nāpi me bhayam āviśat atibhāraṃ tu te manye śālvaṃ keśavanandana
english: The charioteer said: No confusion has entered me, O Janārdana, nor has fear taken hold of me. But I consider Śālva too heavy a burden for you, O son of Keśava.

sanskrit: so 'payāmi śanair vīra balavān eṣa pāpakṛt mohitaś ca raṇe śūro rakṣyaḥ sārathinā rathī
english: "So I withdraw slowly, O hero — this evildoer is powerful, and a warrior who has been confused in battle must be protected by his charioteer.

sanskrit: āyuṣmaṃs tvaṃ mayā nityaṃ rakṣitavyas tvayāpy aham rakṣitavyo rathī nityam iti kṛtvāpayāmy aham
english: "Long-lived one, you must always be protected by me, and I likewise must be protected by you — knowing that a warrior must always be guarded, I have withdrawn.

sanskrit: ekaś cāsi mahābāho bahavaś cāpi dānavāḥ nasamaṃ raukmiṇeyāhaṃ raṇaṃ matvāpayāmy aham
english: "You are alone, O mighty-armed one, while the Dānavas are many. Judging this battle as unequal, O Rukminiya's son, I have retreated.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca evaṃ bruvati sūte tu tadā makaraketumān uvāca sūtaṃ kauravya nivartaya rathaṃ punaḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: While the charioteer spoke thus, then the one whose banner bears the sea-monster, O Kauravya, said to the charioteer: "Turn the chariot back."

sanskrit: dārukātmaja maivaṃ tvaṃ punaḥ kārṣīḥ kathaṃ cana vyapayānaṃ raṇāt saute jīvato mama karhi cit
english: "O son of Dāruka, never do this again under any circumstance — retreat from battle, O charioteer, as long as I am alive, at any time.

sanskrit: na sa vṛṣṇikule jāto yo vai tyajati saṃgaram yo vā nipatitaṃ hanti tavāsmīti ca vādinam
english: "He is not born in the Vṛṣṇi clan who abandons battle, or who strikes down one who has fallen and says 'I am yours.'

sanskrit: tathā striyaṃ vai yo hanti vṛddhaṃ bālaṃ tathaiva ca virathaṃ viprakīrṇaṃ ca bhagnaśastrāyudhaṃ tathā
english: "Likewise one who strikes a woman, or an old man, or a child, or one without a chariot, or one scattered in rout, or one whose weapons and arms are broken.

sanskrit: tvaṃ ca sūtakule jāto vinītaḥ sūtakarmaṇi dharmajñaś cāsi vṛṣṇīnām āhaveṣv api dāruke
english: "And you are born in a charioteer's family, trained in the charioteer's craft, and you know dharma for the Vṛṣṇis even in battles, O Dāruka.

sanskrit: sa jānaṃś caritaṃ kṛtsnaṃ vṛṣṇīnāṃ pṛtanāmukhe apayānaṃ punaḥ saute maivaṃ kārṣīḥ kathaṃ cana
english: "Knowing fully the conduct of the Vṛṣṇis at the forefront of armies, do not make retreat again, O charioteer, under any circumstance.

sanskrit: apayātaṃ hataṃ pṛṣṭhe bhītaṃ raṇapalāyinam gadāgrajo durādharṣaḥ kiṃ māṃ vakṣyati mādhavaḥ
english: "What will the elder brother of Gada, the formidable Mādhava, say to me who has retreated, been struck from behind, and fled the battle in fear?

sanskrit: keśavasyāgrajo vāpi nīlavāsā madotkaṭaḥ kiṃ vakṣyati mahābāhur baladevaḥ samāgataḥ
english: "Or what will Balarama, the elder brother of Keśava, clad in blue, intoxicated with pride, the mighty-armed one, say when he comes?

sanskrit: kiṃ vakṣyati śiner naptā narasiṃho mahādhanuḥ apayātaṃ raṇāt saute sāmbaś ca samitiṃjayaḥ
english: "What will the grandson of Śini, the lion among men and great archer, say about my retreat from battle, O charioteer? And Samba, the victor in battle?

sanskrit: cārudeṣṇaś ca durdharṣas tathaiva gadasāraṇau akrūraś ca mahābāhuḥ kiṃ māṃ vakṣyati sārathe
english: "And the formidable Cārudeṣṇa, and likewise Gada and Sāraṇa, and Akrura the mighty-armed — what will they say to me, O charioteer?

sanskrit: śūraṃ saṃbhāvitaṃ santaṃ nityaṃ puruṣamāninam striyaś ca vṛṣṇīvīrāṇāṃ kiṃ māṃ vakṣyanti saṃgatāḥ
english: "And the women of the Vṛṣṇi heroes, gathering together, what will they say to me who am considered brave, virtuous, and ever proud of manhood?

sanskrit: pradyumno 'yam upāyāti bhītas tyaktvā mahāhavam dhig enam iti vakṣyanti na tu vakṣyanti sādhv iti
english: "'This Pradyumna comes back, frightened, having abandoned the great battle — shame on him!' they will say, and will not say 'well done.'

sanskrit: dhig vācā parihāso 'pi mama vā madvidhasya vā mṛtyunābhyadhikaḥ saute sa tvaṃ mā vyapayāḥ punaḥ
english: "Shame and mockery spoken in words, even for me or one like me, is worse than death, O charioteer. Therefore do not retreat again.

sanskrit: bhāraṃ hi mayi saṃnyasya yāto madhunihā hariḥ yajñaṃ bharatasiṃhasya pārthasyāmitatejasaḥ
english: "For Hari, the slayer of Madhu, having entrusted his burden to me, has gone to the sacrifice of Pārtha the lion of Bhāratas, of immeasurable splendor.

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā mayā vīro niryāsyann eva vāritaḥ śālvaṃ nivārayiṣye 'haṃ tiṣṭha tvam iti sūtaja
english: "The hero Kṛtavarmā, as he was departing, was restrained by me: 'I will hold back Śālva — you stay,' I said. O son of the charioteer,

sanskrit: sa ca saṃbhāvayan māṃ vai nivṛtto hṛdikātmajaḥ taṃ sametya raṇaṃ tyaktvā kiṃ vakṣyāmi mahāratham
english: "And he, the son of Hridika, trusting me, turned back. Having met him after abandoning the battle, what shall I say to that great warrior?

sanskrit: upayātaṃ durādharṣaṃ śaṅkhacakragadādharam puruṣaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ kiṃ vakṣyāmi mahābhujam
english: "When the formidable one bearing conch, discus and mace — the lotus-eyed man, the mighty-armed one — comes back, what shall I say to him?

sanskrit: sātyakiṃ baladevaṃ ca ye cānye 'ndhakavṛṣṇayaḥ mayā spardhanti satataṃ kiṃ nu vakṣyāmi tān aham
english: "And to Sātyaki and Balarama and those other Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis who constantly rival me — what indeed shall I say to them?

sanskrit: tyaktvā raṇam imaṃ saute pṛṣṭhato 'bhyāhataḥ śaraiḥ tvayāpanīto vivaśo na jīveyaṃ kathaṃ cana
english: "Having abandoned this battle, struck from behind by arrows, carried away by you helplessly, O charioteer, I could not live under any circumstance.

sanskrit: sa nivarta rathenāśu punar dārukanandana na caitad evaṃ kartavyam athāpatsu kathaṃ cana
english: "So turn the chariot back swiftly, O son of Dāruka. This must never be done thus, even in adversity.

sanskrit: na jīvitam ahaṃ saute bahu manye kadā cana apayāto raṇād bhītaḥ pṛṣṭhato 'bhyāhataḥ śaraiḥ
english: "I would never value life, O charioteer, if I have retreated from battle in fear, struck from behind by arrows.

sanskrit: kadā vā sūtaputra tvaṃ jānīṣe māṃ bhayārditam apayātaṃ raṇaṃ hitvā yathā kāpuruṣaṃ tathā
english: "When have you ever known me, O son of the charioteer, tormented by fear, abandoning the battlefield and retreating like a coward?

sanskrit: na yuktaṃ bhavatā tyaktuṃ saṃgrāmaṃ dārukātmaja mayi yuddhārthini bhṛśaṃ sa tvaṃ yāhi yato raṇam
english: "It is not fitting for you to abandon the battle, O son of Dāruka, when I am so eager to fight. Go where the battle is."

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca evam uktas tu kaunteya sūtaputras tadā mṛdhe pradyumnam abravīc chlakṣṇaṃ madhuraṃ vākyam añjasā
english: Vāsudeva said: Thus addressed, O son of Kuntī, the charioteer's son then spoke to Pradyumna in battle these smooth and sweet words straightforwardly.

sanskrit: na me bhayaṃ raukmiṇeya saṃgrāme yacchato hayān yuddhajñaś cāsmi vṛṣṇīnāṃ nātra kiṃ cid ato 'nyathā
english: "I have no fear, O son of Rukmiṇī, in guiding the horses in battle, and I am skilled in warfare for the Vṛṣṇis — there is nothing other than that here.

sanskrit: āyuṣmann upadeśas tu sārathye vartatāṃ smṛtaḥ sarvārtheṣu rathī rakṣyas tvaṃ cāpi bhṛśapīḍitaḥ
english: "Long-lived one, the instruction in charioteering is remembered: the warrior must be protected in all circumstances. And you were greatly tormented.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi śālvaprayuktena patriṇābhihato bhṛśam kaśmalābhihato vīra tato 'ham apayātavān
english: "For you were struck hard by an arrow shot by Śālva and overcome by stupor, O hero — that is why I retreated.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ sātvatamukhyādya labdhasaṃjño yadṛcchayā paśya me hayasaṃyāne śikṣāṃ keśavanandana
english: "Now you, the foremost of the Sātvatas, have fortunately regained your senses. Watch my skill in guiding the horses, O son of Keśava's beloved.

sanskrit: dārukeṇāham utpanno yathāvac caiva śikṣitaḥ vītabhīḥ praviśāmy etāṃ śālvasya mahatīṃ camūm
english: "Born of Dāruka and trained properly by him, fearless I now enter this great army of Śālva."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato vīra hayān saṃcodya saṃgare raśmibhiś ca samudyamya javenābhyapatat tadā
english: Having spoken thus, O hero, he then urged the horses in battle and, taking up the reins, charged forward with speed.

sanskrit: maṇḍalāni vicitrāṇi yamakānītarāṇi ca savyāni ca vicitrāṇi dakṣiṇāni ca sarvaśaḥ
english: He executed intricate circular maneuvers, paired and alternating ones, and various leftward and rightward ones on all sides.

sanskrit: pratodenāhatā rājan raśmibhiś ca samudyatāḥ utpatanta ivākāśaṃ vibabhus te hayottamāḥ
english: Struck by the whip, O king, and gathered up by the reins, those finest horses appeared as if leaping into the sky.

sanskrit: te hastalāghavopetaṃ vijñāya nṛpa dārukim dahyamānā iva tadā paspṛśuś caraṇair mahīm
english: Recognizing Dāruka as possessed of lightness of hand, O king, those horses then barely touched the ground with their hooves, as if on fire.

sanskrit: so 'pasavyāṃ camūṃ tasya śālvasya bharatarṣabha cakāra nātiyatnena tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: He circled Śālva's army counter-clockwise, O bull of the Bhāratas, with little effort — it seemed like a wonder.

sanskrit: amṛṣyamāṇo 'pasavyaṃ pradyumnena sa saubharāṭ yantāram asya sahasā tribhir bāṇaiḥ samarpayat
english: Unable to endure being circled counter-clockwise by Pradyumna, that king of Saubha suddenly struck his charioteer with three arrows.

sanskrit: dārukasya sutas taṃ tu bāṇavegam acintayan bhūya eva mahābāho prayayau hayasaṃmataḥ
english: But the son of Dāruka, disregarding that onslaught of arrows, O mighty-armed one, continued onward in harmony with the horses.

sanskrit: tato bāṇān bahuvidhān punar eva sa saubharāṭ mumoca tanaye vīre mama rukmiṇinandane
english: Then that king of Saubha released many various arrows once more at my son, the heroic son of Rukmiṇī.

sanskrit: tān aprāptāñ śitair bāṇaiś ciccheda paravīrahā raukmiṇeyaḥ smitaṃ kṛtvā darśayan hastalāghavam
english: The son of Rukmiṇī, slayer of enemy heroes, cut down those arrows before they reached him with sharp arrows, smiling and displaying his lightness of hand.

sanskrit: chinnān dṛṣṭvā tu tān bāṇān pradyumnena sa saubharāṭ āsurīṃ dāruṇīṃ māyām āsthāya vyasṛjac charān
english: Seeing those arrows cut down by Pradyumna, that king of Saubha resorted to a terrible demonic illusion and released arrows.

sanskrit: prayujyamānam ājñāya daiteyāstraṃ mahābalaḥ brahmāstreṇāntarā chittvā mumocānyān patatriṇaḥ
english: Recognizing the Daitya weapon being deployed, the mighty one countered it with the Brahmā weapon, cutting it apart, and released other arrows.

sanskrit: te tad astraṃ vidhūyāśu vivyadhū rudhirāśanāḥ śirasy urasi vaktre ca sa mumoha papāta ca
english: Those arrows swiftly dispelled that weapon and pierced him, feeding on blood — in his head, chest and face — and he swooned and fell.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite kṣudre śālve bāṇaprapīḍite raukmiṇeyo 'paraṃ bāṇaṃ saṃdadhe śatrunāśanam
english: When that wretched Śālva had fallen, tormented by arrows, the son of Rukmiṇī nocked another arrow, the destroyer of enemies.

sanskrit: tam arcitaṃ sarvadāśārhapūgair; āśīrbhir arkajvalanaprakāśam dṛṣṭvā śaraṃ jyām abhinīyamānaṃ; babhūva hāhākṛtam antarikṣam
english: Seeing that arrow, honored by all the Dāśārhas, blazing like the sun's fire, being drawn to the bowstring — cries of lamentation arose in the sky.

sanskrit: tato devagaṇāḥ sarve sendrāḥ saha dhaneśvarāḥ nāradaṃ preṣayām āsuḥ śvasanaṃ ca mahābalam
english: Then all the hosts of gods together with Indra and the lord of wealth dispatched Nārada and the mighty Wind-god.

sanskrit: tau raukmiṇeyam āgamya vaco 'brūtāṃ divaukasām naiṣa vadhyas tvayā vīra śālvarājaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: Those two came to the son of Rukmiṇī and spoke the words of the gods: "This Śālva king must not be slain by you, O hero, under any circumstance.

sanskrit: saṃharasva punar bāṇam avadhyo 'yaṃ tvayā raṇe etasya hi śarasyājau nāvadhyo 'sti pumān kva cit
english: "Withdraw the arrow again — this one is not to be killed by you in battle. For with this arrow of his in the field, there is no man anywhere who cannot be killed.

sanskrit: mṛtyur asya mahābāho raṇe devakinandanaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ saṃkalpito dhātrā tan na mithyā bhaved iti
english: "His death in battle, O mighty-armed one, has been ordained by the Creator as Kṛṣṇa, the son of Devakī. Let that not prove false."

sanskrit: tataḥ paramasaṃhṛṣṭaḥ pradyumnaḥ śaram uttamam saṃjahāra dhanuḥśreṣṭhāt tūṇe caiva nyaveśayat
english: Then Pradyumna, exceedingly delighted, withdrew that finest arrow from the best of bows and placed it back in the quiver.

sanskrit: tata utthāya rājendra śālvaḥ paramadurmanāḥ vyapāyāt sabalas tūrṇaṃ pradyumnaśarapīḍitaḥ
english: Then Śālva rose up, O king of kings, utterly despondent, and quickly withdrew with his army, tormented by Pradyumna's arrows.

sanskrit: sa dvārakāṃ parityajya krūro vṛṣṇibhir arditaḥ saubham āsthāya rājendra divam ācakrame tadā
english: That cruel one, harassed by the Vṛṣṇis, abandoned Dvārakā and, mounting the Saubha vessel, O king of kings, ascended to the sky.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca ānartanagaraṃ muktaṃ tato 'ham agamaṃ tadā mahākratau rājasūye nivṛtte nṛpate tava
english: Vāsudeva said: When the city of Anarta was freed, then I came back, after the great Rājasūya sacrifice of yours had concluded, O king.

sanskrit: apaśyaṃ dvārakāṃ cāhaṃ mahārāja hatatviṣam niḥsvādhyāyavaṣaṭkārāṃ nirbhūṣaṇavarastriyam
english: And I saw Dvārakā, O great king, with its luster destroyed, bereft of Vedic recitation and vaṣaṭ calls, its noble women without ornaments.

sanskrit: anabhijñeyarūpāṇi dvārakopavanāni ca dṛṣṭvā śaṅkopapanno 'ham apṛcchaṃ hṛdikātmajam
english: Seeing the groves of Dvārakā in unrecognizable forms, filled with doubt, I asked the son of Hridika.

sanskrit: asvasthanaranārīkam idaṃ vṛṣṇipuraṃ bhṛṣam kim idaṃ naraśārdūla śrotum icchāmahe vayam
english: "This city of the Vṛṣṇis appears greatly ill at ease, its men and women unwell — what is this, O tiger among men? We wish to hear."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu sa mayā vistareṇedam abravīt rodhaṃ mokṣaṃ ca śālvena hārdikyo rājasattama
english: Thus addressed by me, the son of Hridika told me all this in detail — the siege and deliverance by Śālva, O best of kings.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ kauravaśreṣṭha śrutvā sarvam aśeṣataḥ vināśe śālvarājasya tadaivākaravaṃ matim
english: Then I, O best of the Kauravas, having heard everything completely, there and then made up my mind for the destruction of King Śālva.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ bharataśreṣṭha samāśvāsya pure janam rājānam āhukaṃ caiva tathaivānakadundubhim sarvavṛṣṇipravīrāṃś ca harṣayann abruvaṃ tadā
english: Then I, O best of the Bhāratas, having reassured the people of the city, King Ahuka and likewise Anakadundubhi and all the foremost Vṛṣṇi heroes, spoke these words gladly.

sanskrit: apramādaḥ sadā kāryo nagare yādavarṣabhāḥ śālvarājavināśāya prayātaṃ māṃ nibodhata
english: "Vigilance must always be maintained in the city, O bulls of the Yādavas. Know that I am setting forth for the destruction of King Śālva.

sanskrit: nāhatvā taṃ nivartiṣye purīṃ dvāravatīṃ prati saśālvaṃ saubhanagaraṃ hatvā draṣṭāsmi vaḥ punaḥ trisāmā hanyatām eṣā dundubhiḥ śatrubhīṣaṇī
english: "I will not return to the city of Dvārakā without slaying him. Having slain Śālva together with his Saubha city, I shall see you again. Let this war-drum, terror to enemies, be struck with the three-sama beat."

sanskrit: te mayāśvāsitā vīrā yathāvad bharatarṣabha sarve mām abruvan hṛṣṭāḥ prayāhi jahi śātravān
english: Those heroes, duly reassured by me, O bull of the Bhāratas, all said to me joyfully: "Go, slay the enemies."

sanskrit: taiḥ prahṛṣṭātmabhir vīrair āśīrbhir abhinanditaḥ vācayitvā dvijaśreṣṭhān praṇamya śirasāhukam
english: Blessed with benedictions by those heroes of gladdened souls, having caused the best of twice-born to recite blessings, and bowing my head to Ahuka,

sanskrit: sainyasugrīvayuktena rathenānādayan diśaḥ pradhmāpya śaṅkhapravaraṃ pāñcajanyam ahaṃ nṛpa
english: With my chariot yoked to Sainya and Sugrīva, filling all directions with sound, I blew the foremost conch Pāñcajanya, O king.

sanskrit: prayāto 'smi naravyāghra balena mahatā vṛtaḥ kḷptena caturaṅgeṇa balena jitakāśinā
english: I set forth, O tiger among men, surrounded by a great force — an organized four-limbed army shining with victory.

sanskrit: samatītya bahūn deśān girīṃś ca bahupādapān sarāṃsi saritaś caiva mārttikāvatam āsadam
english: Passing through many lands, mountains with many trees, lakes and rivers, I reached Marttikavata.

sanskrit: tatrāśrauṣaṃ naravyāghra śālvaṃ nagaram antikāt prayātaṃ saubham āsthāya tam ahaṃ pṛṣṭhato 'nvayām
english: There I heard, O tiger among men, that Śālva had set out from the city nearby, mounted on the Saubha vessel. I followed him from behind.

sanskrit: tataḥ sāgaram āsādya kukṣau tasya mahormiṇaḥ samudranābhyāṃ śālvo 'bhūt saubham āsthāya śatruhan
english: Then reaching the ocean, in the bosom of its great waves, Śālva, O enemy-slayer, mounted on the Saubha vessel, came to be at the navel of the sea.

sanskrit: sa samālokya dūrān māṃ smayann iva yudhiṣṭhira āhvayām āsa duṣṭātmā yuddhāyaiva muhur muhuḥ
english: He, spotting me from afar, smiling as it were, O Yudhiṣṭhira, that evil-souled one challenged me again and again to battle.

sanskrit: tasya śārṅgavinirmuktair bahubhir marmabhedibhiḥ puraṃ nāsādyata śarais tato māṃ roṣa āviśat
english: His city could not be reached by the many marrow-piercing arrows shot from Śārṅga — then anger entered me.
